veranderings.blok: Genoeg, en nie te veel nie
veranderings.voor: op jou bord is nog nie balans nie
veranderings.na: op jou bord beteken nog nie balans nie
veranderings.rede: A noun phrase 'elke groep ... op jou bord' cannot naturally 'be' balance; 'beteken' says what is meant at the same word count.

veranderings.blok: Genoeg, en nie te veel nie
veranderings.voor: van sy ouderdom en grootte en hoe
veranderings.na: van sy ouderdom, grootte en hoe
veranderings.rede: A list of three items takes a comma rather than a repeated 'en'; same word count.
'Drank' on its own easily reads as alcohol; 'drankies' is the natural word for sweet drinks for a Grade 6 learner.
'Dit' could refer back to 'jou liggaam'; naming vesel removes the ambiguity at the same word count.

veranderings.voor: Botter is vet en suikerbone gee ook vesel
veranderings.na: Botter is vet, en suikerbone gee ook vesel
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two clauses with their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.

veranderings.voor: wat die kind gedoen het veroorsaak nie
veranderings.na: wat die kind gedoen het, veroorsaak nie
veranderings.rede: A comma after the embedded relative clause separates its verb 'gedoen het' from the main verb 'veroorsaak' and makes the sentence easier to read.
A disease 'kom' is colloquial; 'ontstaan' is the written form and matches the lesson's own 'kan deels uit 'n swak dieet ontstaan'.
AWS 2017: 'en' joins two clauses with their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.
As a conjunction introducing a clause, written Afrikaans uses 'totdat' rather than 'tot'.

veranderings.voor: Wanneer die liggaam oor 'n lang tyd baie
veranderings.na: 'n Toestand waarin die liggaam oor 'n lang tyd baie
veranderings.rede: A definition opening with 'Wanneer' copies the English 'when ...' pattern; an Afrikaans definition names what the term is; adds two words.
'Ontstaan' is the written form for a disease arising; keeps the glossary consistent with the study text if that change is kept.
